operator_io_quirks: All 7 tables report rows=0: the frozen original is EMPTY, so original_values/original_sizes are all empty/0 and every sampler starts with no elements (p:=1 path).
DDL uses backtick-quoted identifiers and mixed case (`state`, `border_info`, `highlow`); generated SQL must double-quote them.
`country_name varchar(3)` dispatches to String(length=3) via char-family args[0]=3 -> very short random strings, not 3-letter country codes.
`area`/`density` declared `double` -> Number with scale=0 (no args), so ints in [-1,1] plus +-1/+-2 perturbation; not realistic areas.
`highlow.highest_elevation`/`lowest_elevation`/`highest_point`/`lowest_point` are TEXT but semantically numeric -> String fuzzer, no numeric affinity.
`river.traverse` is a single TEXT column FK to state.state_name but semantically a list of states; FK fill gives one state name only.

`border_info` has TWO FKs to the same parent `state` (border, state_name) and a composite PK (border, state_name) -> both columns must draw from state.state_name; self-consistent pairs not guaranteed.
`lake` has NO primary key and NO FK (state_name is a plain text column, not declared FK) -> TS will not tie lake.state_name to state; dangling values expected.
`city` composite PK (city_name, state_name) where state_name is also the FK -> PK dedup and FK fill interact; composite-PK members get max_l0=30.
`mountain` composite PK (mountain_name, state_name) with state_name FK -> same interaction; mountain_name alone is not unique.
`state` is the FK root for city/border_info/highlow/mountain/river; table order puts state at level 0, all others level 1 (lake level 0, no deps).

`country_name NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` on state/city/lake/mountain: TS does not enforce NOT NULL in Python, but String sampler rarely yields NULL, so inserts mostly succeed; empty-string default never used by TS.
operator_ts_expectations: Empty original -> every column sampler has zero elements, so p is forced to 1 and TS draws only fresh random values (no literal-pool anchoring unless train SQL supplies literals).
state.state_name (PK, String) -> random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() of length 0..20, contaminated 50% of the time; no real state names.
country_name -> String(length=3): 0..3-char random strings, so joins/filters on 'USA' etc. never match; likely FN driver for country predicates.
population/area/density/mountain_altitude/length -> Number scale=0: ints in [-1,1] perturbed by +-1/+-2; area/density as tiny ints, implausible -> FN on range predicates (e.g. area > 1000).
highlow text elevation columns -> random strings, so numeric comparisons on them are type-mismatched; SQLite affinity may coerce, driving FP/FN unpredictably.
border_info.border and state_name both drawn from state.state_name with replacement -> many rows where border==state_name (self-border) and pairs not symmetric; FP on 'borders X' queries.
lake.state_name not an FK -> random string unrelated to state.state_name; joins lake-state mostly empty -> FN on lake/state join queries.
river.traverse FK to state -> single state name, so 'river traverses state X' matches at most one state; multi-state rivers impossible -> FN.
Composite PKs (city, border_info, mountain) deduped after fill; with small state cardinality, city rows collapse heavily -> small city tables, FN on counts.
FK fill draws from parent's FINAL filtered column; if state PK dedup leaves few states, child tables get few distinct FK values -> ties/duplicates abundant, FP on DISTINCT/count queries.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python; rows violating constraints are skipped at insert, so actual row counts < requested sizes -> FN on COUNT(*) exact-value queries.
String contamination (prefix/suffix/drop-char) makes equality predicates on names almost never match gold literals -> FN on name = 'X' queries.
